events.description: Osama bin Laden killed in Pakistan; VP Biden says the mission is accomplished and the US should leave Afghanistan
Mullah Omar dies; the Taliban conceal his death until 2015
Taliban nearly disintegrate after Omar's death is exposed; Mullah Yaqoob, his uncle and other factions leave; Sirajuddin and Jalaluddin Haqqani reassemble the Taliban and are rewarded
Khalilzad testifies to Congress alongside Roggio on Pakistan's backing of the Afghan Taliban and the strength of the Taliban-al-Qaeda relationship
Abdul Rahman al-Logari captured in a joint Indian intelligence-CIA operation before a planned suicide attack in New Delhi; handed to the US and imprisoned at Bagram
Doha agreement signed; Pompeo says the Taliban would 'destroy al-Qaeda'
Zawahiri sheltering in Kabul in a Haqqani safe house (as stated by host)
Biden announces unconditional withdrawal; claims the Afghan military is 300,000 strong and well equipped; Taliban declare victory
US abandons Bagram Airfield in early July with al-Logari and thousands of ISKP/al-Qaeda/Taliban prisoners still held there
Taliban take Bagram and open the prisons, freeing thousands of ISKP members, dozens of al-Qaeda members and thousands of Taliban fighters including al-Logari
US military and CIA begin tracking a potential ISIS attack on Kabul airport
ISKP suicide bomber Abdul Rahman al-Logari attacks Abbey Gate, killing 13 US troops and ~170 Afghan civilians while Haqqani Badri 313 provided outer security
Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine; hosts argue the Kabul debacle was the final push for Putin
Biden says al-Qaeda is gone from Afghanistan, contradicting UN reporting of training camps in six provinces
Chinese foreign ministry revives 'Kabul moment' propaganda on the second anniversary of the Taliban taking Kabul

key_claims: The Haqqani Network is an integral part of the Taliban, not a separate entity; Haqqani Badri 313 ran Kabul airport security in Aug 2021.
Sirajuddin Haqqani is a deputy emir, interior minister, and is assessed by many to be an al-Qaeda member who sat on al-Qaeda's executive shura; he hosted Zawahiri in a Kabul safe house.
The Taliban-al-Qaeda alliance never broke; the Taliban stayed out of power for 20 years rather than break it, and some Taliban government members are also al-Qaeda members.

The Haqqanis have a years-long history of facilitating ISKP attacks in Kabul; ISKP leader Ghafari (Shahab al-Muhajir) is a former Haqqani commander; collusion in the Abbey Gate attack was at least possible if not likely.
The Taliban freed thousands of ISKP prisoners from Bagram, including the Abbey Gate bomber al-Logari, about ten days before the attack.
The Haqqanis (Sirajuddin and Jalaluddin) reassembled the Taliban after the 2015 crisis over Mullah Omar's concealed death, when Mullah Yaqoob and his uncle had broken away.
UN reporting shows al-Qaeda running training camps in six Afghan provinces, including training TTP suicide bombers, contradicting Biden's claim al-Qaeda is gone.
The Biden administration's 300,000 Afghan-army figure was knowingly inflated (police and ghost units counted).
